name: BOSU Squat — Eyes Closed
description: A bodyweight squat performed on the dome of a BOSU ball (dome side up) with the eyes closed. The unstable dome surface creates multi-directional instability, and removing the visual input further challenges the proprioceptive and vestibular systems to control the squat movement. This is a high-level proprioceptive challenge used in late-stage ankle, knee, and ACL rehabilitation when functional dynamic balance under load with no visual input is being restored.

execution.starting_position: Stand on the dome of the BOSU ball, feet hip-width apart, centered. Find balance with eyes open first. Have a wall or partner nearby.
execution.setup_instructions: Master BOSU squats with eyes open before attempting eyes closed. ALWAYS have a safety surface or person nearby. Never attempt on an elevated surface.
steps: Step 1: Step onto the BOSU dome and find balance with eyes open.
Step 2: Once stable, slowly close the eyes.
Step 3: Perform a controlled squat to approximately 60-70 degrees of knee flexion with eyes closed, focusing on proprioceptive feedback from the feet and ankles.
Step 4: Return to standing. Open the eyes between repetitions if needed.
execution.breathing_instructions: Breathe normally throughout. Calm rhythmic breathing aids balance and reduces anxiety.
common_mistakes: Attempting eyes-closed before mastering eyes-open BOSU squats
Squatting too deeply too soon — the balance challenge increases dramatically with depth
Tensing the whole body to manage instability — allow the ankle and hip to respond naturally
safety_considerations: ALWAYS have a safety surface within reach — a wall, rack, or partner
If dizziness or significant loss of balance occurs, open the eyes immediately and step off the BOSU
This is for late-stage rehabilitation only — not for anyone with acute balance deficits or vertigo
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: 60-70 degrees of knee flexion is appropriate — do not go to full depth with eyes closed on a BOSU initially.
execution.tempo_recommendations: 3s eccentric, 1s pause at bottom, 2s concentric return.
coaching_cues: Feel the dome through your feet — let the ankle and hip respond to the wobble
Breathe slowly — calm breathing reduces instability
Close the eyes slowly — do not snap them shut
